cards.title: One lap decides the whole sprint
cards.text: 22 cars, three rounds: 6 out after the first, 6 after the second, and ten left to fight for the grid that shapes everything the sprint can become.

cards.title: Russell takes it
cards.text: By 0.068s over Antonelli. Less time than a blink.

cards.title: Out before it got serious
cards.text: Perez (P17), Stroll (P18), Gasly (P19), Bottas (P20), Albon (not classified), Lawson (not classified).

cards.title: So close to the top ten
cards.text: Hulkenberg (P11), Bortoleto (P12), Colapinto (P13), Ocon (P14), Bearman (P15), Alonso (P16, no time set in this round).

cards.title: 10 laps thrown in the bin
cards.text: In qualifying a deleted lap can be the difference between Q3 and going home early.

cards.title: Lindblad and Hamilton were quickest through the trap: 330 km/h
cards.text: Top speed says as much about wing level and the tow from the car ahead as it does about the engine.

cards.title: Nobody owned the whole lap
cards.text: The quickest sectors of the session were split between three drivers, so the ideal lap was never actually driven.

cards.title: Yellow flags out 2 times during the session
cards.text: A yellow in the wrong sector at the wrong moment ends somebody's lap, and sometimes their session.

cards.title: How the sprint starts
cards.text: P1 Russell · P2 Antonelli · P3 Norris · P4 Piastri · P5 Hamilton · P6 Leclerc
bullets: Bearman qualified P15 and starts P19, 4 places further back
Gasly qualified P19 and starts P20, 1 place further back
Bottas qualified P20 and starts P21, 1 place further back
The grid is not the qualifying order. A penalty moves a car back, whether for something on track or for a new engine, and everybody behind it moves up
